desc:
Customer portal development gives your clients a private, branded area where they sign in and see their own orders, invoices, files and updates. Ecom Swift LLC builds the portal on your website and connects it to the records you already keep.

## What is a customer portal?

A customer portal is a secure section of your website where each customer signs in and sees information that belongs only to them. It might show order history, invoice status, project progress, shared documents or support messages. It acts as a self-service counter that is open at all hours.

The key idea is separation. Every customer account is tied to its own records, so one person can never see another person's data. That rule has to be built into the app itself, not just hidden in the design.

## Why customers keep asking for updates

If clients can only learn the status of an order or project by emailing you, your inbox becomes a status board. Each question takes a reply, each reply takes time, and the customer still waits. Files get lost in long threads, and invoices are sent again because nobody can find the first one.

A portal answers the common questions before they are asked. The customer checks the page, sees the current state and moves on. Your team spends less time on routine replies and more on real work.

## How a portal affects your results

A clear portal makes a business feel organized and dependable, which supports repeat orders and longer relationships. Customers who can see their invoices and pay through a link usually settle faster than those who must wait for a reminder. Fewer status emails also means faster answers for the questions that do need a person.

The size of the benefit depends on how many routine questions you receive today. A business that is asked for updates all day gains the most. We build around the questions your customers actually send.

## What a great customer portal includes

- Secure sign-in, password reset and, where wanted, single sign-in with an existing account.
- Strict separation so each customer sees only their own records.
- Record views for the things customers ask about, such as orders, quotes or tickets.
- Secure file downloads, and uploads where customers need to send documents.
- Messages between the customer and your team, kept in one place.
- Email alerts when something changes, with a link back to the portal.
- An invoice list with a payment link, for businesses that bill online.
- An admin screen to add, edit and disable customer accounts.
- An activity log so you can see who viewed or changed what.
- Your logo, colors and wording applied so it feels like part of your brand.

## What we do

We start by listing what your customers ask about and where that information lives today. We then design the views, connect the data from a sheet, an export or a live system, and build login and permissions. Before launch we test with sample customers to confirm no one can reach another account.

The Basic package provides login, one record view and your branding, with data loaded from a sheet or export. Standard adds several record views, secure file downloads, messages and email alerts. Premium adds more record views, live sync with one system, an invoice list with a payment link, an admin screen, an activity log and a handover call. Add-ons include an extra record view, single sign-in and branded email templates.

## What to do and what to avoid

**Do:**
- Start with the three questions customers ask most often.
- Decide who on your team owns each kind of update.
- Keep the data source tidy, since the portal will show it as it is.
- Offer a clear password reset route.
- Test with a real customer account before announcing it.

**Avoid:**
- Showing internal notes or costs to customers by mistake.
- Sharing a single login between several people at a client.
- Loading every old record when only recent ones matter.
- Sending alerts for every tiny change.
- Leaving former customers with active accounts.

## Who it is for

This service suits an agency or studio that wants clients to follow project progress, a wholesaler whose trade customers check orders and invoices, and a service provider who exchanges documents with clients. It also suits a store owner who wants a richer account area than the checkout platform offers.

## What we need from you

Send a description of the information customers should see, a sample of the data or export, your branding and details of any system it must connect to. We never ask for passwords. Access to your systems is given as a collaborator, staff, team or developer user where the platform supports it.
